question.problem:
A Japanese-style table tennis racket is made from a wooden blade covered with rubber on one side.  The weight of a blade is normally distributed with a mean of $80\,\text{g}$ and a variance of $31\,{\text{g}}^{2}.$ The weight of the rubber is normally distributed with a mean of $45\,\text{g}$ grams and a variance of $50\,{\text{g}}^{2}.$ If one racket is randomly selected, what is the probability that it weighs more than $128\,\text{g}?$ You may assume that the weights are independent.

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ | $\,0.04\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.1\,$ | $\,0.5398\,$ | $\,0.5438\,$ | $\,0.5478\,$ | $\,0.5517\,$ | $\,0.5557\,$ |
| $\,0.2\,$ | $\,0.5793\,$ | $\,0.5832\,$ | $\,0.5871\,$ | $\,0.5910\,$ | $\,0.5948\,$ |
| $\,0.3\,$ | $\,0.6179\,$ | $\,0.6217\,$ | $\,0.6255\,$ | $\,0.6293\,$ | $\,0.6331\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Let $X$ denote the weight of the blade, and let $Y$ denote the weight of the rubber. We want to find 

$$
P(X+Y>128).
$$

Since $X$ and $Y$ are  independent random variables such that $X∼N(80,31)$ and $Y∼N(45,50),$ then 

$$
\begin{aligned}X+Y & ∼N(80+45,31+50) \\  & ∼N(125,81).\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variable $X+Y$ is normally distributed with mean $\mu =125$ and standard deviation $\sigma =\sqrt{81}=9.$

In order to find $P(X+Y>128),$ we convert $X+Y$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X+Y>128) & =P(Z>\frac{128-125}{9}) \\  & ≈P(Z>0.33) \\  & =1-P(Z\le 0.33) \\  & =Φ(0.33)\end{aligned}
$$

Using the $z$-table, we see that

$$
Φ(0.33)≈0.6293.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X+Y>128) & ≈1-Φ(0.33) \\  & ≈1-0.6293 \\  & ≈0.3707.\end{aligned}
$$
